Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect both rollout visual views and the inherited controller evidence. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf before proposing any architecture, as required, and record any actual transfer in the policy notes.

The README confirms one editable policy file and a strict provenance requirement: notes must precede the policy edit, durable guidance must materially change, and formal CFD is prohibited. I’m now following the visual-first skill and bookshelf protocol before forming the candidate hypothesis.

The sampled set contains a useful contrast despite four capture terminations: three runs exactly reproduce the assigned-parent controller, while one uses a one-sided target-ray residual and improves the crossing score only marginally. The inherited point-consistent carrier-relief experiment is the clearest negative comparator—it preserved capture and wake appearance but degraded the crossing to the edge of the capture radius. I’m checking both its visual rows and trace diagnostics before deciding what should change.

The evidence favors a feedback-structure change, not more gain tuning. I’m selecting a point-consistent terminal steering confirmation: reconstruct the head’s instantaneous body-frame velocity from the one-step target-vector rate and body yaw, then add bounded steering only when that head-course error agrees with the established course request. It preserves the sampled carrier and never withdraws the yaw-braking signal—the failure mode shared by the symmetric sightline residual and carrier-relief variants. The bookshelf contributes the invariant of sensor-modulating directional work while retaining the propulsive rhythm; no published gains or kinematics are being transferred.

The candidate and durable lesson are now in place. The controller changes only the terminal observation/feedback path; all propulsion, reserve allocation, soft-envelope, speed, reallocation, and stopping-risk mechanisms remain intact. I’m validating syntax, parameter ownership, finite bounded outputs, and the required workspace contract without running CFD.

The required check-runner role could not start because its configured validation model is unavailable in this account. I did invoke it as required; I’m now reading its local check specification and executing those same deterministic checks directly so validation can still complete.

Two deterministic checks pass: the guidance update is materially semantic, and only the authorized policy file differs under `solver/`. The Julia contract command is presently blocked because `julia` is not on this environment’s PATH; I’m checking for the workspace’s pinned runtime and independently auditing the same schema/finite-output conditions.

Validation is complete to the extent supported by this workspace: the required guidance and boundary checks pass, all 33 referenced parameters are declared, the policy contract occurs exactly once with balanced syntax delimiters, and an exact parent-trace replay confirms the new residual is finite, bounded, sign-preserving, and terminal-only across 60 samples. No CFD was run. The only unavailable check is Julia execution itself because no Julia runtime is installed or discoverable here.

I found the pinned Julia runtime outside the module launcher and reran the exact required smoke command successfully. All three prescribed checks now pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract with finite two-joint output, and solver edit boundary.

Implemented exactly one target-policy candidate.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): adds bounded, terminal-only, point-consistent head-course confirmation.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:234): adds the reusable lesson distinguishing one-sided confirmation from failed steering withdrawal and carrier relief.

All prescribed checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, parameter ownership, finite two-joint output, and solver boundary. No CFD was run.
